items.description: The University's video surveillance infrastructure has reached a critical point in its lifecycle, with core recording servers, storage arrays, and centralized management hardware now exceeding six years of service. items.title: UT Tyler Student Financials Business Affairs Project
items.description: This project will develop a student-level tuition revenue reporting solution that provides comprehensive visibility into student financial activity and net tuition revenue. The report will include key student and financial attributes, including: Unique Student Identifier (EMPLID) Academic Term Academic Level Academic Group / School Discounts & Allowances Total Net Tuition (Net Revenue) A primary objective of this initiative is to establish and document the official Finance-approved methodology for identifying and calculating Discounts & Allowances. The project will evaluate existing Student Financials and Finance processes to determine whether these classifications can be derived from ITEM_TYPE_CD, specific ITEM_TYPE values, or other business rules and accounting methodologies maintained by the Finance team. As part of the analysis, the project will review and assess existing reporting assets, data models, mappings, subject areas, calculations, and business logic currently used across Student Financials and Finance reporting. Areas of focus include: Tuition Revenue Mandatory and Optional Fees Waivers Discounts & Allowances Net Tuition / Net Revenue The project will also identify any existing reports, financial models, or reporting frameworks that already classify and summarize these transactions. Where appropriate, established Finance-approved logic will be leveraged to ensure consistency, reduce duplication of effort, and align reporting results across institutional systems and stakeholders. The expected outcome is a standardized and validated reporting solution that provides accurate student-level tuition revenue metrics while aligning with existing Finance methodologies, accounting practices, and reporting standards.

items.title: Voice Infrastructure Modernization
items.description: The University of Texas at El Paso's current Voice Central Infrastructure relies on legacy Primary Rate Interface (PRI) telecommunications services and aging Ribbon SBC2K Session Border Controllers that were deployed to support campus voice communications. While this platform has provided reliable service, the technology is approaching the limits of its operational lifecycle and no longer aligns with modern telecommunications standards, cloud communications strategies, or carrier network evolution. To ensure the continued reliability, security, and scalability of university voice services, Information Resources proposes a modernization initiative to migrate all PRI-based voice connectivity to SIP Trunking services and replace the existing Ribbon SBC2K infrastructure with the latest generation Ribbon Session Border Controller hardware. This initiative supports UTEP's long-term communications roadmap and aligns with industry best practices for unified communications, Microsoft Teams Voice integration, business continuity, and cloud-based telecommunications. The migration to SIP Trunking will eliminate dependence on legacy circuit-based telecommunications services and transition the university to an IP-based architecture that provides greater flexibility, improved disaster recovery capabilities, and simplified carrier connectivity. SIP services offer enhanced scalability, allowing the university to rapidly adjust call capacity as institutional needs evolve without requiring costly physical circuit installations. Simultaneously, replacing the aging Ribbon SBC2K appliances with current-generation Ribbon hardware will provide increased processing capacity, modern security protections, enhanced resiliency, and long-term vendor support. The new platform will strengthen connectivity between carrier services, Microsoft Teams Voice, Avaya systems, analog gateways, emergency communications infrastructure, and future cloud voice services while improving operational reliability across all campus locations. Existing planning documents already identify the replacement of Ribbon SBC infrastructure as part of the university's technology refresh strategy and future SIP implementation plans.

items.title: Prevent changes in T&E profile from being overridden
items.description: The chartfield default for an employee's T&E module is related to the chartfield used for their payroll. Sometimes the T&E chartfield should be different, but when we attempt to change this, PS overrides the change. As a result, the default chartfield that is communicated to Concur is incorrect. This is related to ticket INC0018634. The following information was placed in that ticket by the developer. We met with the HCM and FSCM dev teams to review the programming logic and have concluded the following on how the Travel Profile is being updated. To retrieve UTZ_FE153_CHARTFIELD funding details from IB to send to FMS Travel Profile: 1. Process selects employee record from Job (selects most effective dated row) 2. Position Number is retrieved from Job record. 3. Position Number is then used to retrieve the chartfield string values from the Department Budget Table (DBT) 4. Max distribution percentage from Budget details is selected if there are multiple rows. 5. If employee is funded by Project ID, the Project ID is ignored and is not sent to FMS My suggestion would be at this point that if you do not want the process to override the changes in TnE, a new enhancement request would have to be created.

items.title: Cherwell Project HCM-1509 Secure 2.0 Act
items.campus: UTA, UTD, UTEP, UTRGV, UTSA, UTT, UTPB, UTSHARE
items.description: The Secure 2.0 ACT was signed into law on December 30, 2022. It made a multitude of changes to public retirement plans across the country. 1) Applies to any participant whose previous year W-2 Box 5 field reflects a salary of $145,000 (to be indexed annually) or higher. a. If a participant is subject to this requirement, then any catch-up dollars beyond the base limit must be made on an after-tax (Roth) basis. b. Only impacts participants whose previous year W-2 meets criteria. Will not impact new employees who did not have a previous year W-2 from UT. 2) Campuses must establish a process to identify impacted participants. a. Campuses should also continue their programming work to ensure the paychecks deduct appropriately. b. OEB is partnering with Retirement Manager to ensure programming is in place to assist with this process. VOLUNTARY CHANGES as voted on by BAC: 1) Elimination of Special Catch-Ups as of 1/1/2026. a. By a unanimous vote of the Benefits Advisory Committee, the 15-year service Catch-Up on the UTSaver TSA 403(b) plan will be removed. b. Likewise, the Special Catch-Up feature of the UTSaver DCP 457(b) plan will be removed. c. Campuses will need to be able to identify any participants who are using the Special Catch-Ups in 2025 for special direct communications before 2026. 2) Addition of Age-Band Catch-Ups a. Secure 2.0 added a new age-based catch-up of $10,000 (or 150% of the age-50 catch-up) for any participants ages 60-63. b. This catch-up does not require any calculations and will be programmed into UT Retirement Manager for eligible participants. It will operate in the same way as existing age-50 catch-ups. c. Please ensure programming is in place at your institution to permit the age-band catch-up remittances by the December 2025 payroll that produces the January 2026 paychecks. i. It is OEB’s understanding that all major HR and payroll systems are programming for this feature, often as a default. Check with your Peoplesoft, Workday or Oracle support. ii. Retirement Manager will have the age-band limit programming in place and sample file formats will be shared in 2025 for institutions who wish to use Retirement Manager’s limit enforcement capabilities.

items.title: Automate Match Workbench Voucher Error Notifications
items.description: With resources continuing to be strained, UTA is exploring opportunities to automate system driven notifications to reduce manual effort and improve operational efficiency. Within Accounts Payable, vouchers with match exceptions require user action before payment can proceed; however, users are not consistently or clearly notified when these errors occur. Upon review of the Match Workbench, UTA identified an existing notification capability that can alert users when vouchers contain match errors. Testing in Production confirmed that this functionality is already configured, but it is not currently automated or optimized for regular use. When notifications are sent, they rely on numeric error codes that do not clearly explain the issue, limiting their effectiveness. This issue primarily affects departmental users responsible for resolving voucher issues, as well as Accounts Payable staff who must manually monitor match exceptions and follow up when vouchers remain unresolved. As a result, vouchers may sit in error status longer than necessary, contributing to delayed payments and increased manual workload. This idea was triggered by the need to improve visibility into match errors, reduce reliance on manual follow up, and support more timely payment processing. Addressing this problem now allows UTA to better leverage existing system functionality, improve user understanding of match issues, and mitigate payment delays without introducing significant customization.
